MENTOR PROSE (in an answer turn this is a slip; the learner sees only the answer): The speed graph shows how fast a property changes between two keyframes. In Mentor Practice, any layer with its own keyframes can be opened in it. Title's Position is one example.

- **Height means speed.** A curve along the bottom means the layer isn't moving there.
- **Easing shows as slopes.** A curve that climbs slowly after a keyframe is an ease out. One that drops slowly into the next keyframe is an ease in.
- **Handles shape the curve.** Drag a keyframe's handles to change it. Longer handles give a stronger ease.
- **Distance and timing stay the same.** The area under the curve doesn't change, so the layer still covers the same distance in the same time. Only the speed along the way changes.

- You drag a key's handles to shape the curve. Longer handles give a stronger ease.
